findings.evidence: Roadmap JacobianChallenge/README.md:96 lists Cl(X) ≅ Pic X; deferral flagged in Dedekind.lean:34-35 and FractionalIdealDivisor.lean:38-39,176-177. Existing bridge fractionalIdealDivisorAddEquiv + fractionalIdealDivisor_toPrincipalIdeal (FractionalIdealDivisor.lean:179-181) already gives the comparison by quotient descent. classGroupComap signature (PrincipalComap.lean:85) returns (S.comap φ).ClassGroup →+ S.ClassGroup, not ClassGroup R.
findings.fix: Either land this together with the actual Cl(X) ≅ ClassGroup R construction that consumes classGroupComap (demonstrating the dependency is real), or have a human add 'functoriality of the order-system class group in the value group' to the roadmap first; the roadmap's only functoriality target (Layer D, README.md:174) is contravariance in the curve, a different notion.
findings.issue: New capability (contravariant functoriality of OrderSystem in the value group G: comap, classGroupComap surjection, transport lemmas) that main lacked. The stated target Cl(X) ≅ ClassGroup R is real and deferred, but the visible path to it is a quotient descent of the existing AddEquiv fractionalIdealDivisorAddEquiv (which already carries toPrincipalIdeal x to principalDivisor x, FractionalIdealDivisor.lean:179-181); it does not go through comap/classGroupComap. classGroupComap's codomain is an OrderSystem.ClassGroup (a WeilDivisor quotient), never ClassGroup R (a fractional-ideal quotient), so it cannot be the comparison map. No in-tree consumer of comap/classGroupComap exists.

summary: Single coherent topic, but this is new functoriality of the OrderSystem class-group construction in the value group G, and its only justification is the deferred Cl(X) ≅ ClassGroup R comparison, which is reached by descending the already-existing fractionalIdealDivisorAddEquiv to quotients — a path that does not use comap/classGroupComap. Structurally classGroupComap's codomain is an OrderSystem class group, never Mathlib's fractional-ideal ClassGroup R, so it cannot be the comparison map; the tie to the target is analogy, not a proximate prerequisite.
